# SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE: a fictional decision, not a real case

Harlow v. Fenwick Township, 2031 XXSC 77

Reasons for Judgment

[1] The township applies for an injunction restraining the respondents from obstructing the north access road, with a term directing the police to arrest and remove any person who breaches it.

[8] The respondents erected a barrier across the north access road on three occasions between March and May, and on each occasion remained after being asked to leave.

[12] An enforcement term directing the police to arrest and remove persons who breach an injunction is extraordinary. It is included only where there is evidence that the order will otherwise not be obeyed and that the ordinary contempt process will not suffice.

[13] Here, the respondents returned to the road three times after being asked to leave, and the township's two contempt applications did not end the obstruction. The ordinary contempt process has not sufficed, and I include the enforcement term.

[15] In Abbott v. Birch, 2019 XXCA 101, the court said that an injunction should never issue against unnamed persons. Neither party addressed that decision, and I need not decide whether it applies here.

[18] A court may limit an enforcement term to a defined area and period. The barrier stood only on the north access road, and I limit the term to that road for six months.

[20] The respondents gave no undertaking to stay off the road, and their spokesperson told the court they would return. Without an undertaking the risk of renewed obstruction is real, and I grant the injunction for the full term sought rather than the shorter term the respondents proposed.
